issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to be a no-argument method returning a String (signature messageOnMilk(): String), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) with a double parameter. This parameter mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion: template Main calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments, and the UML/specification show a no-arg method, so students implementing according to the spec/template would not match the solution's interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to declare messageOnMilk() with no parameters (String messageOnMilk()) and update Seal and Goat implementations to match the no-arg signature and expected return format, or (B) update the problem statement and template (including Main) to specify and use messageOnMilk(double volume). Prefer option A to align with the UML and existing template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters that returns a String (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). The solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) and the implementing classes (Seal, Goat) implement a version that requires a double parameter and returns a string including the volume. This mismatch changes the method signature and return format for the same conceptual action (milking an animal), causing students to be unable to map the required API in the problem/template to the solution implementation and leading to compilation or behavioral confusion (the template's example calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API across artifacts. Preferably change the solution to match the problem/template: modify Milkable to declare String messageOnMilk() with no parameters, and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if the volume argument is intentional, update the problem statement and template examples to require/illustrate messageOnMilk(double volume) and adjust the expected return format consistently.
